cards.explanation: The free space is at the end of nums1, so writing there never clobbers unread elements.

incorrectOptionExplanations.From the front (smallest first): Would overwrite unread elements of nums1.

promptVariants: Why is writing at k never going to overwrite an unread element of nums1?
Why can't filling nums1 from the back clobber elements that have not been merged yet?
cards.answer: k = i + j + 1 always points at or beyond i (the next unread element of nums1) because j >= 0 slots of nums2 remain; so the slot being written is free or already consumed.
cards.explanation: That is the key correctness claim of the backward merge.

cards.explanation: Each pointer moves in one direction once.

promptVariants: Extra space of the backward merge: ___

Why does the loop run only while j >= 0, and why can the remaining nums1 elements be left alone?
cards.answer: Once nums2 is exhausted the remaining nums1[0..i] elements are already in their final positions (the front of the array), so nothing more is needed. If nums1 is exhausted first (i < 0) the else branch copies the rest of nums2.
keyPoints: Leftover nums1 prefix is in place
